title: Gold Is Getting Crushed—Is This The Start Of A Bigger Downturn? | Jeff Christian
speaker: Jeff Christian (CPM Group)

macro_themes.view: 10y-2y flattening signals weakening economy but is a poor recession timer; recession likely sometime before 2028, possibly 2027 and shallower than feared.
Rates rise because of inflation and debt, which are more positive for gold than higher rates are negative; 5% 10y with 3.4% inflation is only ~1.6% real.
Expects at least one, maybe two more Fed hikes, dependent on a weakening economy.
Big Beautiful Bill spending cuts in Q4 2026-early 2027 and a nasty midterm environment will hurt US growth.
Dollar and gold can both rise as havens; not surprised if both keep rising over the next several years.

calls.reason: Secular bull market intact: debt, inflation and unprecedented geopolitical risk; central banks and value buyers step in around 3,800-4,100.
calls.quote: from a fundamental longer term perspective, the gold market is still very much in a bull market

notes: Recorded Monday Sept 28 ("today on the 28th of September"), gold down ~3.5% intraday at ~4,100. Short-term direction not given; he notes short-term traders are bearish. No view on TNX direction beyond not being concerned about 5%.
